bug_semantics: ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) accepts C (file) and nested D (directory) record names from the remote SCP protocol stream, extracts the server-controlled filename without validation, and combines it with currentDirectoryFullName. A malicious, compromised, or MITM server can supply ../ components or an absolute/drive-qualified path so Directory.CreateDirectory or FileInfo.Open/Create operates outside the caller's destination, enabling arbitrary file creation or overwrite wherever the client process can write. Exploitation requires the victim to initiate a recursive directory download from the attacker-controlled endpoint.
flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the initial ScpClient feature commit: d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 added recursive SCP download parsing and both local filesystem sinks, directly concatenating the untrusted D/C record filename below currentDirectoryFullName with no plain-name or containment check. Later commits only restyled, moved, or refactored these already-vulnerable lines.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object check: `git cat-file -p d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3` identifies both author and committer as `olegkap_cp <olegkap@gmail.com>` at Unix time 1323285149 and contains only the three-line message `Minor fix to ASCIIEncoding`, `Add ScpClient to support SCP feature with limited featres supported in silverlight and WindowsPhone environment`, `Add ScpClient test`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistant, or bot marker.
evidence: First-party GHSA-q939-rpr3-3284 states the affected API is `ScpClient.Download(string directoryName, DirectoryInfo directoryInfo)`, the attack is a malicious/compromised/MITM SCP server returning traversal or absolute names, affected versions are >= 0 and <= 2025.1.0, patched version is 2026.0.0, and remediation commit is 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce.

At 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce^ (c66b9f8fb06c12e71761e58a577b1e796026310f), `src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs` parses `${filename}` from DirectoryInfoRegex/FileInfoRegex and passes it unvalidated to `Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.Combine(currentDirectoryFullName, filename))` and `new FileInfo(Path.Combine(currentDirectoryFullName, fileName))`, after which the file is opened with FileMode.Create/FileAccess.Write.

`git show 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce -- src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs` shows the direct closure: it adds EnsureValidLocalName and invokes it immediately before both Path.Combine sinks. The helper rejects empty, `.`, `..`, and any character in Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars, covering separators and platform-specific drive qualifiers before filesystem access.

`git blame` of the pre-fix sinks first points to the 2023 merge/refactor 42ff9206d22d90af4083ffe8483276daee289bfe; inspecting that commit shows it moved the same InternalDownload implementation out of ScpClient.NET.cs, so it is not the BIC. Blaming the pre-move file points through the 2016 line-ending-only commit 57a78fc3a42632c1709b3537a43c982d0e8462dc to d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3. `git log -L` reaches d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3, and `git log --reverse -S 'currentDirectoryFullName, Path.DirectorySeparatorChar, fileName' -- Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs` returns d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 first, followed only by the 2017 syntax conversion 266dbaefe6c1f2bff2ea00c9ac14a246d37079d9.

`git show d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 -- Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs` shows the new 276-line ScpClient.NET.cs containing the recursive directory-download parser and the two unsafe local path constructions. `git rev-list --parents -n 1 d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3` gives sole parent 96c512fddb159ef2821342c956111a0fac86a984, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 96c512fddb159ef2821342c956111a0fac86a984 -- Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs` produces no paths, directly proving parent absence.

The BIC is an ordinary one-parent feature commit, not a merge, revert, move, release/backport, or reconstructable squash: its parent has no ScpClient files and the commit adds the implementation and tests in one Git object, so there are no member SHAs to decompose.

Release ancestry is reproducible with `git tag --contains d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3`, which includes every repository release tag from 2016.0.0-beta1 through 2025.1.0. Tag 2025.1.0 resolves to 6390ede31e0101dad1d09bcb98e6dc9a0741c89a; tag 2026.0.0 resolves to 7b2fd3dbf2c86a80a7b06cea020aa5f821c9902e. `git tag --contains 600be0de543765995a189b5d7cd4efac5007f3ce` returns only 2026.0.0, establishing the vulnerable/fixed tag boundary and matching the advisory's <=2025.1.0 / 2026.0.0 boundary.

`git cat-file -p d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3` is the sole AI-evidence source used: human-named author/committer olegkap_cp, identical non-bot email, 2011 timestamp, and no AI attribution or generation trailer. The 2026 fix commit's authorship and any later history were not used for the AI verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is rooted in the original recursive-download implementation, not in later refactors: d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 first created the SCP C/D record-to-local-path dataflow, while its direct parent has no ScpClient implementation at all. The advisory fix directly guards both sinks and first reaches release 2026.0.0 after vulnerable 2025.1.0. Because the BIC commit object identifies a normal human author/committer and contains no AI/bot marker, the causal code introduction is NOT_AI.
